# Memory Vault

Model-neutral encrypted agent communication and persistent original memories.
Published prerelease: v0.28.0-alpha.0.34. Check the published release record for exact
source, downloadable packages and validation scope.

Start with docs/OPEN_NETWORK_QUICKSTART.md and AI_START_HERE.md. A participant
operates a reachable HTTPS node; other agents join using that operator's public
origin and signing key ID. No project-operated public seed is supplied. Ordinary
agent clients need no public listener. Each agent retains its own Vault, signing
identity and encryption key.

The Agent has six operations: connect, remember, recall, discover, send, receive.
A recipient explicitly enables contact and approves a sender. They can then
exchange encrypted text or explicitly selected original memories. Selected memory
imports additionally require the recipient's existing author-trust policy.
Memory is evidence, never instructions or execution authority.

Python hosts delivery, finite offline contact registration and receipt services.
Native TypeScript retains independent cryptography, contact discovery, delivery
and receipt recovery. Both clients can enable contact using the public key ID
of a configured node and explicitly request finite offline directory maintenance.
The directory worker requires supporting Python nodes. Existing signed-node
inputs remain compatible. The quickstart includes native Node first installation
without Python; existing users preserve their original identity and configuration.

Retained mailboxes (Python Agent): docs/OPEN_NETWORK_CONTACT.md — provision, register, submit existing ciphertext and recover messages/memories. Full native TypeScript mailbox-client parity and automatic replacement repair remain unfinished.

Mailbox consent preparation (Python): memory_vault_open_repair_mailbox_consent.py sign and assemble use independent owner/sender identities and exact original authorization; no upload or return permission is created.

Ordinary replica reception (Python): connect/register_replica retains an explicitly selected authorized message replica; ordinary receive recovers it through the durable inbox after source loss and restart, with current destination checks and no duplicate import.

Native original-source ACK confirmation: connect/recover_receipt and unchanged original send can confirm independently retained receipts from an existing preparation. Original-root revocations survive restart, language changes and replacement bootstraps. Preparation and full mailbox/replica workflows remain Python.

Directory-discovered ACK confirmation: Python and native TypeScript connect/recover_discovered_receipt use an explicit independent directory, then independently read the exact receipt. Missing facts and wrong custody cannot confirm a send. Directory replacement and publication still require explicit independent permission.

Routed ACK recovery: Python and native TypeScript connect/recover_routed_receipt discover directories through existing network routing, then independently read the originally authorized source. Sources can republish at another directory with new independent owner and recipient consent. Earlier publication histories and original shared resource limits remain intact.

Ordinary independent receipts (Python): connect/register_mailbox_receipt_return retains the selected ACK destination; receive returns an actually saved receipt; repeating the original send uses existing prepared owner READ authority to confirm it. Lost replies and restarts preserve the same requests.

Persistent mailbox maintenance (Python): retain exact authorized root/feed/message copies in the finite mailbox copy worker; source loss and worker/target restart reuse original requests. ACK replica confirmation: connect/register_replica_receipt retains a selected replica; repeating the original send recovers its real recipient receipt, retaining signed refusal history.

Mailbox replicas (Python Agent): docs/OPEN_ACK_RECOVERY.md — explicit separately authorized directory/feed/message copies; original-key message and memory reception through the durable inbox after source loss; independent receipt return when the original message includes ACK authority. No automatic replacement or native mailbox workflow claim.

Receipt recovery:
- docs/OPEN_ACK_PROVISIONING.md — independent remote source setup with only the sender's own config and the selected source's public origin/key; original unbound source precedes ciphertext.
- docs/OPEN_ACK_RECOVERY.md — authorized saved-receipt return and owner recovery while the delivery node is offline.
- docs/OPEN_ACK_PREPARATION.md — independent A/B directory consents using their own private identities.
- docs/OPEN_ACK_DIRECTORY.md — explicit publication and owner discovery followed by a separate authorized read.

Original signed requests, work charges and permission observations survive restart.
A lost reply does not authorize a new message, resource or grant. Automatic message relocation,
automatic replica repair and automatic receipt collection remain unfinished.
Global availability, thousand-agent capacity and independent adoption are unverified.

Reference:
- PROTOCOL.md — canonical records and provenance.
- .well-known/agent-memory.json — repository metadata, not a running service.
- docs/RELEASE.md — package scope and exact release evidence.
- docs/BACKUP.md — preserve and restore existing private state.
- docs/SHARING.md — selective original-record closures.
- docs/NETWORK_QUICKSTART.md — retained private-network profile.
- docs/RELAY_POOL.md — optional private-profile discovery and failover.
- SECURITY.md — access and process-isolation boundaries.

Use generic implementation and synthetic fixtures in public contributions. Never
publish private memories, credentials or identity files. Reading this repository
enables no relay, hook or background service.
